clue.text: An enchanting head-covering

parts.note: one who enchants is a charmer, and a light lacy scarf or feathered headpiece shares that name, so the clue describes both at once

explanation.surface: A hat so lovely it casts a spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for someone who captivates is also the name of a decorative headpiece or lace head-scarf, so 'enchanting' does double duty in the reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A lacy scarf or small decorative headpiece is called by the same word as a charmer who captivates.

clue.text: Surface in foot — one

indicators.note: in places the word for one inside the abbreviation for foot

parts.note: an ace is a one on dice or cards

explanation.surface: A single step placed on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts ACE inside FT.
explanation.definitionFit: A face or flat side of a cut gem is one surface of it.

clue.text: Without science the street-cleaner would be a vindictive type

parts.note: sc is an abbreviation for science
someone bent on revenge is an avenger

explanation.surface: A street sweeper without education turns vengeful.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says that taking SC (science) away from the answer leaves AVENGER; put together, SC and AVENGER spell a street sweeper in old usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An old term for a person employed to clear refuse from the streets, now more often a creature feeding on carrion.

clue.text: What perfect ladies, for a change!

indicators.note: for a change says the letters of the word ladies are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Perfect women, just this once!
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a change' rearranges LADIES; the definition is 'What perfect', meaning standards of perfection.
explanation.definitionFit: Models of perfection or principles one aims at are things considered flawless.

clue.text: A doctor as unhappy with gold as a diplomat

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
taken as written
unhappy means sad
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A gloomy doctor posted abroad as an envoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unhappy' looks like an anagram signal but just means SAD; MB is Bachelor of Medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior envoy representing a state in a foreign country.

clue.text: A sound piece of work.

parts.note: a musical composition is literally a work made of sound, and also a solid achievement

explanation.surface: A well-made job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'solid', but means music: a composer's numbered work carries this Latin word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for work names a numbered musical composition.

clue.text: This paper put to bed ?

definitions.meaning: a kind of writing paper with a ribbed texture from the wires of the mould
placed down to sleep, past tense of the verb meaning to set down

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor asks whether tonight's edition has gone to press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put to bed' is newspaper slang for sending an edition to print, which makes 'paper' look like a newspaper; it is a type of writing paper instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribbed writing paper carries this name, and a child placed in bed has been set down, the past tense of lay.

clue.text: Keep clear of an empty space

parts.note: the article an gives the letter A
a void is an empty space

explanation.surface: A warning to stay away from a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition, a verb, is split by the wordplay into A VOID.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun or steer away from something is to keep clear of it.

clue.text: He makes up for your complaint

definitions.text: He makes up for your complaint

parts.words: He makes up for your complaint
parts.note: a chemist makes up medicine to treat an ailment, not compensating for a grievance

explanation.surface: A man apologises to atone for your grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes up for' suggests compensating, and 'complaint' a grievance; read instead as a pharmacist who makes up a prescription for an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist who prepares and hands out medicines to patients.

clue.text: Stranded silver ring ?

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a round is a circle or ring

explanation.surface: A silver ring left high and dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship stuck on the bottom in shallow water is beached and stranded.

clue.text: Hunt for a groovy way to decorate

definitions.meaning: to pursue, as hounds do a fox
to engrave or emboss metal by cutting grooves into it

explanation.surface: Searching for a hip new style of home decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groovy' looks like sixties slang for fashionable, but here it means literally making grooves: metalwork engraved this way is said to be chased.
explanation.definitionFit: A pursuit is a hunt, and metalworkers ornament silver by engraving grooves, a craft with the same name.

clue.text: A blockhead, our little boy is, in the middle class

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of the word block
taken as written
Geo is a short form of the boy's name George
taken as written

explanation.surface: A snobbish remark about a dim little lad who belongs to the middle class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blockhead' reads as an insult, a dunce, but it means the head of 'block', its first letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-class conventional tastes and values are summed up by this French-derived adjective.

clue.text: Like a plain family without branches?

definitions.text: Like a plain family without branches?

parts.words: Like a plain family without branches?
parts.note: an open plain has no woodland, and a family with no relatives branching off would lack a family tree, so both readings describe being without trees

explanation.surface: A dull family with no offshoots in its line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective meaning ordinary, but it is the noun, open grassland with no woods; 'branches' points both to boughs and to family lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Grassland with no woods has no trees at all, and so does a family without a genealogy chart.

clue.text: The silly creature's in the soup!

definitions.text: The silly creature's in the soup!

parts.words: The silly creature's in the soup!
parts.note: a fool or simpleton has the same name as a strip of pasta, and 'in the soup' also means in trouble

explanation.surface: Someone foolish has landed in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' is an idiom for being in a mess, but literally it is where a strip of pasta floats; that pasta and a fool share one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is old slang that matches the name of a ribbon of pasta found floating in broth.

clue.text: Dance with a sailor before everyone returns

parts.note: tar is a familiar word for a sailor
ante is Latin for before

indicators.note: returns means the word for everyone comes back, written in reverse

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A sailor dances before the whole crew comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' turns ALL into LLA, which ends the answer after TAR and ANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirling Italian folk dance from Taranto, once thought to cure a spider's bite.

clue.text: Animals' crocks

definitions.meaning: farm beasts kept in a sty
in Scotland and the north, earthenware pots or jars

explanation.surface: Earthenware bowls set out for farm animals to eat from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crocks' suggests broken-down old things, but here it means earthenware pots, called by the same name as sty animals in Scots usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sty-dwelling swine share their name with the Scots word for an earthenware jar or pot.

clue.text: Specious form of blue lapis

indicators.note: form of says the letters are made into a different shape, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A fake version of a blue gemstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' rearranges BLUE LAPIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeming reasonable or true on the surface while possibly false, a near-synonym of specious.

clue.text: Such a festivity bad the noble knight

definitions.text: Such a festivity bad the noble knight

parts.words: Such a festivity bad the noble knight
parts.note: Sir ... of the Round Table begins with this festive occasion, as if the knight's name were the festivity followed by the word had

explanation.surface: A grand celebration held by a chivalrous knight.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'bad', almost certainly 'had': Sir Galahad, the purest Arthurian knight, splits as a festive occasion followed by HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A festive celebration or special public occasion, such as a sports carnival or swimming meet.

clue.text: In Ethiopia a head for drink

definitions.meaning: the title of the emperor or king of Ethiopia
a hot mixture of port or sherry with sugar and spice

explanation.surface: An Ethiopian leader asks for something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ethiopian royal title and the spiced hot wine named after Colonel Francis Negus are the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ethiopian monarch's title matches the name of a mulled wine punch from the eighteenth century.

clue.text: March of the Hippies ?

parts.note: a stiff-legged parade step with the legs swung high from the hip, as if hippies were on parade

explanation.surface: A protest parade of flower children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hippies' sounds like flower children on a protest march, but the clue means a military march that swings the legs high from the hips.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff-legged military parade step, the legs kicked straight out from the hip.

clue.text: Dog on wheels ?

parts.note: to dog is to follow stealthily, and a police patrol car on its rounds does the same

explanation.surface: A puppy riding a skateboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like the animal but is the verb, to stalk; one who skulks around, or a car that does so, fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or vehicle that stalks around stealthily, perhaps planning a crime.

clue.text: Clothes-horse with outspoken grievances?

definitions.meaning: a frame on which washing is hung to dry
someone who voices complaints publicly, one who airs them

explanation.surface: A model who complains loudly about her treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes-horse' suggests a vain dresser, but here it is the frame for drying laundry; to air grievances is to voice them, so a complainer is one who airs.
explanation.definitionFit: A drying rack for washing shares its name with a person who voices or ventilates complaints.

clue.text: Gold, a pound, it is said

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone claims gold sells at a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the phrase 'it is said', describing something spoken rather than written.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spoken by mouth rather than in writing, like a viva examination.

clue.text: Same as before, the old city looks grim

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same as before
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An ancient city still looks as bleak as it ever did.
explanation.walkthrough: DO, short for ditto, is the list-keeper's mark for repeating what came above; UR is Abraham's ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: A stern, sullen and unsmiling manner is called this, a synonym for forbidding.

clue.text: How to address one boat-man coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Harris is one of the Three Men in a Boat in Jerome K. Jerome's novel

explanation.surface: Asking how one should speak to an approaching boatman.
explanation.walkthrough: Harris is one of Jerome K. Jerome's Three Men in a Boat; 'coming up' reverses him in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic contemptuous form of address to a man or boy, as in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Weather-vane substitutes used by suckers

definitions.meaning: a straw thrown up shows which way the wind blows, standing in for a weather-vane
drinking tubes through which liquid is sucked

explanation.surface: Makeshift wind indicators that only fools would rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suckers' looks like dupes, but means those who suck up drinks; the first sense comes from the idiom 'a straw in the wind'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin hollow stalks show wind direction when tossed up, and the same tubes are sipped through for drinks.

clue.text: Lift beams, say

indicators.note: say means the word for beams is to be pronounced, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Lifting heavy wooden beams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beams' looks like timbers to be lifted, but means rays of light.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift or hoist something upwards.

clue.text: Red tints could be harsh

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could be something else when rearranged, signalling a shuffle

explanation.surface: Bright red colours can be garish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' turns RED TINTS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A grating, loud or jarring sound is described with this synonym for harsh.

clue.text: It's the 18th.

parts.note: the puzzle appeared on the eighteenth of the month, so the date referred to is the day of publication

explanation.surface: A simple statement of the date.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue states the date the puzzle was printed, so the answer is the day you are reading it.
explanation.definitionFit: The present day, the date on which the newspaper was being read.

clue.text: Furnished for a season

definitions.meaning: provided or supplied, as in furnished with the loan of something
the forty days of fasting before Easter in the Christian year

explanation.surface: A flat let with furniture for one season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Furnished' suggests a fitted-out flat, but means supplied or loaned; the season is the Christian fast before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Given on loan is a sense of supplied, and the Christian fast before Easter is a church season.

clue.text: The new missus fit only for gaol?

parts.note: a newly married wife is a bride
fit means healthy, in good health

explanation.surface: A grumbling husband says his new wife belongs in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridewell was a London prison, and the name came to mean any house of correction; 'fit' is the adjective meaning healthy, not 'suitable'.
explanation.definitionFit: A former London house of correction gave its name to jails and reformatories generally.

clue.text: How the artist boy is assessed?

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
Ted is a boy's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: Wondering how a young painter's work will be judged.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist.
explanation.definitionFit: To be judged or valued at a certain level is a synonym of evaluated.

clue.text: Gaunt's England, otherwise

parts.note: John of Gaunt's speech in Shakespeare's Richard II calls England this other paradise, so 'otherwise' hints at the word other before the garden

explanation.surface: How a dying duke described his country in other terms.
explanation.walkthrough: John of Gaunt calls England 'this other Eden, demi-paradise' in Shakespeare's Richard II.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's patriot likened his country to the biblical paradise garden of Adam and Eve.

clue.text: A pretty sash perhaps for a Scots dance

indicators.note: perhaps says these two words might become something different when their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Wearing a lovely sash to a Highland dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals a rearrangement of PRETTY SASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow Highland reel from Speyside, named after the valley of the river Spey.
